x: In addition, Bob Readman took third prize in the individual handicap and so brought his tally of awards up to five in four open races. We are expecting big things of him at 10 and 20 miles next season.

With the slowing of Green, our need for a fourth man became apparent, and here Bob Readman came into prominence and completed our team. This was his first "National 20," and reflects the greatest credit on him.
Our fourth man, as last year, was Bob Readman, scoring 28, who did well over such a hilly course. Roberts, competing in his first big race for us, was 44th, Harley 57th and Ted Saunders 68th.

Bentley and Rickards were among those who retired, but we are always assured of a first-rate performance from these two loyal team men when the National Championship comes along. The handicap prize went to Sutton with 9 min. 30 sec. allowance, Bob Readman and Syd Roberts taking the minor placings.

He was closely followed by Bob Readman, who was also placed second in the sealed handicap. Third to finish was Jack Bidgood, and our team was completed by Captain Charlie Churcher in fifth position, and we had six in nine.

Of those other than the scoring team, Charlie Churcher and Bob Readman were always handy, ready to make a really big effort if called upon. Jack Rutland and Joe Coleman, both taking part in their first "National," performed creditably and gained experience, which will probably take them into the fir…
Roberts and Bob Readman. However, as in most long walks, things didn't work out as well as expected.
Roberts led the "Bels." home, closely followed by Bill Snell, Jack Bidgood and Bob Readman. Good packing, but not quite near enough to the front.
Percy Wright, Syd Roberts and Bob Readman, we shall be able to field a good team. Colin Sutton also is getting fit since his return from Canada and may also be able to help, duties permitting.

The longer distance apparently suited our walkers, the scoring three being Bod Readman, Syd Roberts and Bert Webb. All three showed considerable improvement over recent performances, and in addition to winning the scratch race, the same three comprised the 2nd Handicap Team, and Syd Roberts was plac…

With Roberts 2nd, Bob Readman 8th, Percy 11th, and Jack Bidgood 15th, we totalled 36 pts. to the 47 of Surrey W.C. In addition to the scoring four, Jack Rutland and Tug Wilson completed the course inside the time standard of 3 hours 20 minutes.
Our successes were largely due to the leadership of our two captains, Tom Carter and Bob Readman. Both have set their respective sections fine examples by brilliant individual performances.
Pat Larking writes that he feels that his association with the Club will be a happy one, and that Sergeant Bob Readman has been most encouraging (good old "Sarge").
Bob Readman walked splendidly to finish second to Staker in the Middlesex. Had the race been over the pre-war distance of ten miles, Bob may have done even better.
Bob Readman as our only walker to complete 7 miles in the hour.
Bob Readman and Harry Rouse finished second and third respectively in the Police Ten and the following Saturday we met with success in the Surrey County Race, R.
Bob Readman unfortunately had a bad time, and although Jack Rutland, Tommy Green and Joe Wilson walked extremely well, we only managed to tie for third place in the Scratch Team Race.

The entry of 137 was the largest of the season up to that time and the race resulted in a double scratch and handicap win, Syd Spencer gaining a well-deserved success in the individual handicap. In addition to this, Bob Readman was second in the handicap and F.

In the Inter-Club match at Motspur Park on 31/8/46 against strong opposition and without the assistance of our track champion and Bob McMullen, both on holiday, we scored another success, Joe Coleman and Jack Rutland finishing second and third respectively, backed up by Bob Readman in seventh position.

Jack Rutland, on returning to the common, then went up into second place, and with McMullen, Joe Coleman, Len Fletcher and Bob Readman not far behind it soon became apparent that, barring a number of accidents, we should add one more to our list of successes.
Once again the team race was never in doubt, with four of our men in the first 10, backed up by Bob Readman and Charlie Churcher close behind, our final score being 20 points to Highgate Harriers 33.

Joe Coleman dropped back in the later stages of the raec allowing Bob Readman to take the third position. Jack Rutland had previously stated that he intended to retire early in the race owing to a bad cold the week before, and judging by the race in general, we had every hope of making our presence…

In the postponed Woodford Green Open the following week we were without Harry and Charlie Churcher, and although our lads were well placed, with Bob Readman (3rd) leading them home, we could only get second to the promoting club who naturally were out in full strength.
Bob Readman won the Met. Police 10 miles Walking Championship at Imber Court on February 24th, and a month later was second in the National Police Championship.

In all, 40 Walkers started, including 25 of our members, a promising start for the new season. In the absence of Harry Churcher, Bob McMullen led the field, followed by Bob Readman and Smith of the Police.
Outstanding was Bob Readman who held the lead throughout the greater part of the race, but on the last lap he tired rather badly and dropped back to third place.
The walking judges were soon busy and among those making a premature return to the dressing room were Bob Readman of the Home club and Fred Barrett of Cambridge.

Backed up by Bert East, Bob Readman and Bert Clayton, we once again succeeded in winning the scratch team race. The race marked the return of Jack Rutland to racing after a long break, and although he was fairly well down the field, it was pleasing to see him out once again.
Warr who is improving quickly, but the hero of the day was Bob Readman who although feeling the effects of the National Police Championship two days previously battled to the finish to score for us.

Bob Readman, 1st in the M.P.A.A. 10 Miles Championship and 3rd in the National Police 10 Miles Championship. The team of Belgrave Policemen who won the M.P.A.A. 10 Miles Team Championship—Sapcote, Evans, McGreechan and Atkinson.
All our lads started fairly steady and at three miles Charlie Churcher and Bob McMullen were in 5th and 6th positions, whilst Bob Readman and George Oliver were together at 15th.
Oliver was now 8th and Rutland 9th, Bob Readman, seemingly taking it easy, 10th, and Tony Bellchamber, also walking his first 20 very strongly, 11th.
Incidentally, George Atkinson's father was the first individual winner in this race. Bob Readman (6th) and George Bentley (11th) gave us 7 in the first 16 out of a finishing field of 66.

Tebbutt, introduced by Bob Readman, won the Police 6 miles novices race at Regents Park on September 30th in the very fast time of 53 mins. 31 secs. and should prove a great asset to our “ Garnett ” Cup team this season.
Syd James was well up, with McMullen, Bob Readman and Bert Clayton constituted our team. Gerald Warr had a battle with Gordon Waddingham and George Oliver.
Bob Readman, still showing good form, was a popular third, with Captain Charlie fourth. Our Juniors showed up quite satisfactorily and we have great hopes of a win in the coming “Garnet” Cup race.

In the Middlesex race our Cadogan members turned out in full strength and apart from the loss of Bob Readman, who was unfortunately disqualified, all walked exceedingly well and finished 2nd to Highgate Harriers, the first time Cadogan had reached this position since before the war.

Bob Readman continued his long run of Police successes by winning the 7 miles Inter-District championship on January 6th. He followed this up on February 22nd by winning the Police 10 miles championship in the second fastest time ever recorded, 80 mins. 11 secs., only 52 secs. outside Jim Morris's record.

George led the Belgrave team home to victory, this time in a decisive win over Woodford, and in so doing, he was backed up by three other police members, Bob Readman, Hugh McGreechan and Jack Bidgood.

After five miles the front positions were the same, and we had Percy Wright lying handy in the first twenty, with Jack Rutland and Bob Readman walking shoulder to shoulder, and Hugh McGreechan, Harry Shields and Jack Bidgood all packing well in that order.

Veteran Bob Readman, more properly described as " Evergreen," also walked well to finish third. Jack Bidgood, last year's winner, took the Veteran's prize, and the second and third teams in the championship consisted wholly of our members.
Our scoring four are to be congratulated on their splendid team work and we must certainly mention Bob Readman who, although walking in the "B" team, gave good support to our next four, H.

At 6½ miles, the two Georges, Oliver and Beecham, after their excellent County performances, were in 29th and 31st positions, with Hugh McGreechan 33rd, Garry Warr 38th, George Checkley 43rd, Percy Wright 44th, Harry Kemp 58th, Bob Readman 72nd, and Bernard Eglington 77th.
Belgrave were well represented in the Marches with five members in the Police team (Bob Readman, Syd Spencer, Len Demmon, Charlie McLennan and Don Fotheringham) and myself in the R.W.A.
The handicap was won by Eric Hall with Evergreen Bob Readman 2nd, and Doub and Ron Fairman tying for third place. The match resulted in a win for us by 235 points to 295.

Harry after a not very good day, finished 27th with evergreen Bob Readman 42nd, Bill True 49th, Syd Spencer 63rd and Cyril Yescombe 66th. Since this event Cyril has shown considerable improvement and looks like being an asset to the team next year.
Len Demmon trailed the Captain home in 3.13.13 with Bob Readman and Bill True just behind, followed by Cyril Yescombe continuing to show improvement.

At the moment most of our distance men have a Middlesex qualification and our team consisted of George, Bob Newson, Hugh McGreechan, Len Demmon, Bob Readman, Fred Rolfe and Cyril Yescombe, and of course Harry Shields.

Bob Readman, Sid Spencer, Gerry Plaice and Cyril Yescombe were noticed having a steady training spin, probably discussing the advantages or disadvantages of Constabulary duties and civilian life, and Bernard Stevenson had a few behind him this time.
Vickers (Scr) 14.39 and 3.Bob Readman (5.15) 14.45.
Bob Readman, now retired from the Force, was on the road and at the prizegiving was presented with a memento of his past services to the Police Walking Section.

Other positions were Ted Smith 10th, Ray Switzer 18th, Harry Shields 21st Bob Readman 22nd, D. Russell 27th, Nick Milsum 28th, Wally Emery 29th and veteran Bert East 34th, totalling 11 of the 39 finishers.
George Webb gained his 6 mile badge, whilst Bob Readman only just missed his 7 mile. Surely Bob has earned the name "Evergreen"- a grand effort.
Dave just pipped Williams for the handicap with Bob Readman a popular 3rd. What a pity Bob's new job prevents regular attendance, our youngsters could benefit from him.

Walking Championship at Battersea was one of our police stalwarts of the thirties and forties, BOB READMAN. A former Club 20 miles Champion, Bob also won police championships including one at National level.

Casting their eyes on the present and up-and-coming walkers were Charlie Churcher and Bob Readman. With the alterations to Belgrave Hall in mind it is well to recall how much work Charlie put into the present structure so we hope to see him at our HQ when the alterations are complete.
READMAN BOB
Seen at a recent Police Dinner was Bob Readman, one of our many police walkers of the past, a former Club Champion and team member. Now living in Sussex, he sends his regards to old friends.
Bob Readman, Fulham

In addition, Bob Readman took third prize in the individual handicap and so brought his tally of awards up to five in four open races. We are expecting big things of him at 10 and 20 miles next season.
